data.description:
## Observation

On 2026-10-28 at 17:47:26 PDT (2026-10-29 00:47:26 UTC) the kernel killed the on-box `rebar-mcp` process for exceeding its container memory limit (bug teenage-unquieted-ringworm; the memory side is fixed in 451212e377a). Docker restarted the container in place (`restart=always`, same port 8092). What followed:

- nginx answered `/mcp/` with 502 from 00:47:27 to at least 00:47:53 UTC (`upstream prematurely closed`, then `connect() failed (111)`, then `recv() failed (104)`). The first non-502 `/mcp` response was at 00:48:14 UTC. The outage lasted 27-47 seconds.
- Claude Code 2.1.308 (session a85e3cd3, its `mcp-logs-rebar` log) logged 3 "Terminal connection error"s, closed the transport, and then made 5 reconnection attempts at 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and 8 s backoff. All 5 got 502, the last at 00:47:43 UTC, 16 s after the kill. It then logged "Max reconnection attempts (5) reached, giving up".
- That session made no further connection attempts. Every rebar tool call it made afterwards failed with "MCP server 'rebar' has disconnected": 21 calls between 2026-10-29 00:51 UTC and 2026-10-31 01:03 UTC, while the server was healthy and serving other clients.

So one server crash leaves every connected Claude Code session disconnected until a human runs `/mcp` reconnect. The client's 16-second retry window is shorter than the container's restart time. An agent in such a session sees an opaque "disconnected" error and cannot distinguish it from a server outage.

## What the evidence rules out

- Credentials: the PAT file has been unchanged since 2026-09-14, and an authenticated `initialize` returns 200 on 2026-10-31.
- Store divergence (topnotch-brazen-slug): the failure is at the transport layer (502 / connection refused), before any store access.
- Blue-green cutovers: cutovers on 2026-10-30/31 produced no 4xx or 5xx on `/mcp`. The server runs StreamableHTTP without per-session state (`Terminating session: None`).

## Expected

A crash-restart of the MCP container should not outlast a standard client's reconnect window, or the edge should hold or answer requests during the restart instead of returning 502.

## Candidate directions (for planning, not decided)

- Restart into the blue-green standby slot, or keep a warm standby, so nginx fails over (`proxy_next_upstream`) instead of returning 502 while the killed slot restarts.
- Shorten the time from container start to accepting traffic. On 2026-10-31 it took about 22 s (container start 14:34:37 UTC, cutover 14:34:59 UTC).
- Document the operator remedy (`/mcp` reconnect) in docs/mcp-client-setup.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After an induced crash of the MCP process on the box, `/mcp` returns no 502 to clients, or recovers within 15 s, measured from the nginx access log.
- [ ] A Claude Code client connected during the crash is connected again without manual `/mcp` reconnect, shown by its mcp-logs.
data.title: MCP container crash-restart outlasts Claude Code's 16 s reconnect window, leaving sessions disconnected until manual /mcp
